# Two different questions

The package provides two monthly summary functions. They answer different
questions and should not be used interchangeably.

- \`MonthlySummaryTable()\`: what were the monthly statistics in **each
  individual year**?
- \`ClimateSummaryTable()\`: what is the **average monthly climatology across
  years**?

Both functions expect the long-format data returned by \`ImportWeather()\`.

# Monthly summaries by year

```{r, eval = FALSE}
weather <- ImportWeather(
  "data/crossnacreevy.xlsx",
  start_date = "2018-01-01",
  end_date = "2024-12-31"
)

monthly_by_year <- MonthlySummaryTable(weather)
monthly_by_year
```

The result contains one row per year and weather variable, with calendar months
as columns. January 2020 and January 2021 remain separate rows.

# Long-term monthly climate summaries

```{r, eval = FALSE}
climate_normals <- ClimateSummaryTable(weather)
climate_normals
```

The climatology function first calculates each year's monthly statistic, then
takes the mean of those yearly values for each calendar month and variable.
For rainfall, for example, it averages annual January rainfall totals; it does
not average all individual January daily readings across the entire period.

# Aggregation rules

| Variable type | Monthly statistic within each year | Across-year climatology |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Rainfall and daily light totals | Sum of daily values | Mean of yearly monthly totals |
| Daily maximum temperature | Maximum daily value | Mean of yearly monthly maxima |
| Daily minimum temperature | Minimum daily value | Mean of yearly monthly minima |
| Other variables | Mean of daily values | Mean of yearly monthly means |

# Missing observations

Missing values are excluded from a calculation. If a year-month-variable group
contains no observed values, its monthly result is \`NA\`. Climate summaries
exclude missing yearly monthly values from the across-year mean; if every year
is missing for that month and variable, the climatological result is \`NA\`.

Neither function fills missing dates or adjusts for unequal observation
coverage. For comparisons, inspect the number of valid observations in each
year and month and consider whether the source data are sufficiently complete.

# Choosing a function

Use \`MonthlySummaryTable()\` to compare specific years, investigate unusual
seasons or prepare annual reporting tables. Use \`ClimateSummaryTable()\` when
you want a long-term seasonal profile. Always report the years included and
review coverage before interpreting climate differences.
